robustness.alt: The pass rests on a handful of days: without the 5 days where the model did best, the edge falls from +0.17 bp to +0.03 bp; without the top 10 it reverses, to −0.04 bp. The model did better on 87 of 169 days, about half: its edge comes from a few large wins, not from being better on most days. By type of day and by quarter-end window: ordinary (147 days) and outside the quarter-end window (157 days) can't be told apart from zero; month-end (14 days), quarter-end (2 days), tax date (6 days) and inside the quarter-end window (12 days) have too few days to say (under 20 each). Chart: the mean paired difference with its interval for All days +0.17 bp, Ordinary +0.15 bp, Month-end −0.13 bp, too few days, Quarter-end +0.51 bp, too few days, Tax date +1.31 bp, too few days, Outside the quarter-end window +0.11 bp, Inside the quarter-end window +1.07 bp, too few days. Then the mean after dropping the best days: 0 days dropped +0.17 bp, 1 days dropped +0.11 bp, 5 days dropped +0.03 bp, 10 days dropped −0.04 bp.
